description: Successor on the natural numbers with one fixed extra point is injective and omits zero, but the natural-number copy is a proper successor-closed subset containing zero and is exactly the recursive sequence's image.
signature:
Lemmatheca.Entry.NaturalNumbersAsSets.extra_point_counterexample :
  Function.Injective Lemmatheca.Entry.NaturalNumbersAsSets.extraPointSucc ∧
    (∀ (x : WithTop ℕ), Lemmatheca.Entry.NaturalNumbersAsSets.extraPointSucc x ≠ 0) ∧
      (have A := Set.range fun n => ↑n;
        0 ∈ A ∧ (∀ x ∈ A, Lemmatheca.Entry.NaturalNumbersAsSets.extraPointSucc x ∈ A) ∧ A ≠ Set.univ) ∧
        (fun n => Lemmatheca.Entry.NaturalNumbersAsSets.extraPointSucc^[n] 0) = fun n => ↑n
